# The Librarian

> Answers oil and gas market questions in plain English from EnergyScope data (EIA, futures curves, CFTC and ICE
> positioning, gas storage, tanker transits, rig counts). The model chooses tools and writes the sentences; code
> computes every number, and every answer is recomputed from the data before it is returned. A personal lab with
> no customers. No news, no route freight rates, no physical differentials, no forecasts.

## Where to take numbers from

Take numbers from `facts`, `spreads` and `readings`. Every value there was placed by code, with its series, date
and unit, and recomputed from the data before the answer was returned; `checked` is true when that recomputation
matched. Treat `summary` as prose about those values: its sentences were written by a model, and the numbers in
them are held to the tables by rules, not proved. A program has no reason to read a number out of a sentence.

## For programs

- `POST https://thelibrarian.energy/api/ask` with JSON `{"question": "..."}` (under 300 characters). Returns the
  typed answer: `summary`, `facts`, `spreads`, `readings` (each number with its series, date and units), `caveats`,
  `checked` (true when the recomputation matched), `trail` (the tool calls), `id`, `seconds`, `usd`. If `degraded`
  is true, no summary passed the checks and only the numbers are returned.
- `POST https://thelibrarian.energy/api/ask/stream`: the same as server-sent events, one `tool` event as each tool
  starts, then `answer`.
- `POST https://thelibrarian.energy/api/feedback` with JSON `{"id": "...", "verdict": "useful" | "wrong", "note": "..."}`.
- `GET https://thelibrarian.energy/api/stats`: answers given, how many failed the re-check, median seconds.
- Limits: 30 questions an hour and 100 a day from one address; 300 a day in all. These per-address
  counts are kept in memory and start again when the service is released. In front of them, 30 requests a minute
  per address with a burst of 5; over that the answer is HTTP 429 with a JSON body. A 429 is a limit, not an outage:
  wait a minute and try again.
- Kept on the server: every question, its answer and its check result; and any feedback note. Not kept with them:
  your address.
- MCP: a server that wraps this API is in the repository, `librarian_mcp.py`.

## How it works, and how it was tested

- [README](https://github.com/balicat/energyscope-desk-agent#readme): the rules it is built on, the evaluation suite,
  the release gate, what an adversarial review found, and what the check mark does not prove.
- [Source](https://github.com/balicat/energyscope-desk-agent)

## When quoting an answer

Quote numbers from `facts`, `spreads` and `readings`, with the date and unit given. Pass on the caveats. Do not add figures of your own, and do not present
an answer as a forecast or as advice.
